en.title: Uli Latukefu Reportedly Cast as The Legend of Zelda's Ganondorf
en.summary: The live-action adaptation of Nintendo's iconic adventure game is reportedly adding a formidable presence to its cast. Australian actor Uli Latukefu is said to be stepping into the powerful boots of the franchise's ultimate antagonist.
en.body:
The epic journey to bring **The Legend of Zelda** to the silver screen continues to add key players behind the scenes, with a significant new report emerging about its central villain. Australian actor **Uli Latukefu** is reportedly set to portray the formidable **Ganondorf** in the upcoming live-action film, a move that has sent ripples of excitement through the dedicated fanbase.

While official confirmation from Nintendo and Sony remains pending, sources close to the production have informed Deadline that Latukefu, known for his roles in **Black Adam**, **Alien: Covenant**, and the **Young Rock** series, will embody the ultimate antagonist of Hyrule. The distinction between playing 'Ganondorf' rather than 'Ganon' itself is a detail that speaks volumes to those deeply familiar with the franchise's lore. This typically refers to the more humanoid, often regal, and powerfully built Gerudo King before he fully succumbs to his beastly alter ego. This suggests the film might lean into the character's complex history and imposing presence, a vision that some fans have affectionately dubbed 'hansomedorf.' Of course, the terrifying transformation into his monstrous pig-like form is a hallmark of the character, and speculation abounds as to whether this cinematic iteration will showcase that iconic, albeit terrifying, evolution.

## Hyrule's Nemesis Takes Form
The casting news arrives as the film is rumored to have already wrapped production, yet concrete details about the cast have been scarce, adding an air of mystery to the project. The inclusion of **Uli Latukefu** as **Ganondorf** is a crucial piece of the puzzle, promising a compelling confrontation for the film's heroes, **Link** and **Zelda**, who are reportedly being brought to life by **Benjamin Evan Ainsworth** and **Bo Bragason** respectively. Director **Wes Ball** is at the helm, aiming to translate the magic and adventure of the beloved video game series into a live-action spectacle. The anticipation is palpable, as fans eagerly await a definitive look at how this legendary villain will be realized on screen.

## The Triforce of Anticipation
For fans of **The Legend of Zelda**, the casting of **Ganondorf** is more than just another actor joining a movie; it's the selection of the force that has driven so much of the franchise's conflict and drama for decades. This character represents the ultimate evil, the embodiment of power and ambition that Link must constantly overcome. The choice of **Uli Latukefu**, a performer with a commanding physical presence and a growing resume, suggests a deliberate effort to create a villain who is both physically imposing and capable of conveying the gravitas that **Ganondorf** demands. The community is buzzing with theories about his performance and how he will embody the iconic Gerudo King, eager to see if he can capture the essence of a character who is as central to the Zelda mythos as the titular princess or the courageous hero himself.

## What's Next
The **Legend of Zelda** movie is currently slated for a theatrical release on April 30, 2027. Further official casting announcements and glimpses of the film are expected as the release date approaches.

The report that he is playing Ganondorf rather than Ganon (the exact differences between the two is an incredibly nerdy topic we’re happy to save for another day) is perhaps telling in and of itself. Namely, this version of the villain is traditionally a muscular, more humanoid figure that one Reactor team member has dubbed “hansomedorf.” Of course, Ganondorf almost always transforms into a giant pig monster of considerable power and proportions when he’s about to lose a fight, so let’s not rule out any possibilities just yet. Speaking of which, it’s worth noting that The Legend of Zelda movie has supposedly finished wrapping and we still have very little confirmed information regarding most of the movie’s cast . It figures to be a fairly sparse fantasy film so far as the overall cast size goes, though it’s nice to hear that Link will face off against at least one familiar face. The only question now is how much CGI the film’s team will use to bring Ganondorf to life. Physically, Uli Latukefu seems more than capable of playing the role with little visual effects help, though time will tell if we’re lucky enough to get a slightly more natural take on the character that showcases some truly spectacular makeup and costuming. In any case, we’re still waiting on confirmation of this casting announcement, which should hopefully come before The Legend of Zelda movie is released on April 30, 2027.
